title: Der Körper
summary: Body vocab and the two pain patterns — Kopfschmerzen and the first live dative, mir tut ... weh

blocks.title: Körperteile
blocks.body: The words you need when something hurts. Note the articles — they don't follow a pattern, so learn each word with its article.

blocks.title: Tap to hear each body part
Ich habe ... schmerzen
blocks.body: Glue a body part straight onto **Schmerzen** (pain) and you've made a new word: *Kopf* + *Schmerzen* = **Kopfschmerzen** (headache). Then just say **ich habe** + the compound, no article needed: *Ich habe Kopfschmerzen*. Same pattern gives *Halsschmerzen* (sore throat), *Bauchschmerzen* (stomachache), *Rückenschmerzen* (backache), *Zahnschmerzen* (toothache).
blocks.callout: *Halsschmerzen* — Hals and Schmerzen, glued together like every German compound.

blocks.prompt: How do you say 'I have a sore throat'?
blocks.explain: Compound nouns glue together: Hals + Schmerzen = Halsschmerzen. Then it's just ich habe + the compound, no article.

blocks.title: Mir tut der Kopf weh — the dative arrives
blocks.body: A second way to say it hurts uses the **dative** — German's next big case. **wehtun** is actually a separable verb, just like the ones from last week: *weh* jumps to the end. Pattern: **[Dativpronomen] + tut/tun + [Körperteil, Nominativ] + weh**. *Mir tut der Kopf weh* (My head hurts — literally 'to me the head hurts'). The verb agrees with the body part: singular *der Kopf* → **tut**; plural *die Beine* → **tun**.
blocks.callout: *Mir tun die Beine weh* — plural body part, so tun, not tut.

blocks.title: Two ways to say it hurts

pairs.left: Ich habe Kopfschmerzen. — I have a headache.
pairs.right: Mir tut der Kopf weh. — My head hurts.
pairs.note: Both are correct and natural. Ich habe ...schmerzen names the ache as a thing; mir tut ... weh points the dative pronoun straight at the person feeling it.

pairs.left: Mir tut der Rücken weh. — singular, so tut.
pairs.right: Mir tun die Beine weh. — plural, so tun.
pairs.note: wehtun agrees with the body part doing the hurting, not with mir.

blocks.explain: wehtun is separable — the dative pronoun (mir) comes first, weh splits off to the end: Mir tut der Rücken weh.

blocks.hint: Dative pronoun first, then der Rücken, then weh at the end (wehtun is separable).
blocks.explain: Mir tut der Rücken weh — mir (dative) + tut (3rd person singular) + der Rücken (nominative subject) + weh (separable prefix, jumps to the end).
